claim: Antitrust plaintiffs satisfy the predominance requirement for class certification by using a damages model that estimates damages attributable to the antitrust injury on a class-wide basis, even if individualized determinations are later needed to allocate damages among class members.
initial_reasoning: The citation to In Re Bystolic Antitrust Litigation supports the claim because courts have accepted the use of damages models to estimate class-wide damages in antitrust cases, as seen in this litigation. This approach allows for the satisfaction of the predominance requirement under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(b)(3). The key legal basis is the principle that a damages model can demonstrate predominance of common issues over individual ones, even if some individualized determinations are necessary for damage allocation.
